label: early input steps (t=2-4) after o/p/q/z appeared in the prefix
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, almost entirely at t=2-4 (t=2 holds 54% of mass, t=3 36%). Never fires at t=0, on the <DEL> step, or anywhere in the copy phase. Within that window it depends on token identity in a graded, distributed way. Rates are highest when o, p, q or z appeared earlier (prev2_tok o is 7.3x, first_tok o/p 5.3x/4.4x) and when the current input is z, 0, c, o, e or f, and it mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token. Top activations look like o o [z] or p p [?] [z]. The predicate captures 94% of activation mass but has only about 12% precision. Adding the current-token set raises dev F1 to just 0.35, so the selectivity looks like a fuzzy linear mix of token contributions that no simple rule captures. The activation also tends to persist for a step or two after a strong hit, decaying.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev2_tok=q (+3.57), prev2_tok=o (+3.57), prev_tok=z (+3.27), prev2_tok=z (+3.19), prev2_tok=p (+3.07), prev_tok=o (+3.04). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.64), in_tok=p (-4.84), prev_tok=i (-4.54), prev_tok=d (-4.31).
